# Definitions

## Glossary of Terms

### **Downscale Parameters**:

  - **Global Climate Models (GCMs)**: The climr App uses 13 GCMs that are individually useful and are a good representation of the full CMIP6 ensemble - a collection of climate simulations produced by GCMs in a coordinated international climate modelling effort. The recommended defaults used within the app are an 8-model ensemble (ACCESS-ESM1.5, CNRM-ESM2-1, EC-Earth3, GFDL-ESM4, GISS-E2-1-G, MIROC6, MPI-ESM1.2-HR, and MRI-ESM2.0), a selection informed by a sensitivity analysis specific to British Columbia which evaluated the models' ability to capture historic climate variables, as well as other factors such as having multiple runs available. This recommended ensemble is also more consistent with the IPCC's assessment of climate sensitivity than the full 13-model ensemble available (<a href="https://rmets.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/joc.7566" target="_blank">Mahony et al. 2022</a>).
  
  - **Shared Socio-economic Pathways (SSPs)**: Scenarios of future greenhouse gas emissions, these pathways have been built by experts to examine how global society, demographics and economics might change by 2100. The climr App uses projections from the four major SSP scenarios: 
  
    - **SSP1-2.6**: Represents strong action to reduce emissions, in line with the Paris Climate Accords goal of keeping global warming to 2°C above pre-industrial temperatures.
    
    - **SSP2-4.5**: Represents moderate action to reduce emissions, roughly consistent with current emissions policies and economic trends.
    
    - **SSP3-7.0**: Represents a broader range of scenarios where little to no climate policy is implemented, leading to a steady, linear rise in greenhouse gas emissions over time.
    
    - **SSP5-8.5**: Represents a high-emissions scenario driven by rapid expansion in greenhouse gas emissions over the next several decades, resulting in end-of-century emission levels more than three times higher than current emissions.
    
For more information regarding climate model and scenario selection, see <a href="https://bcgov.github.io/climr/articles/guidance_ensembleSelection.html" target="_blank">here</a>.

### **Climate Variables**:
  
  - AHM: Annual heat/moisture index (annual)
  
  - bFFP: Beginning of the frost-free period (day of year) (annual)
  
  - CMD: Hargreaves climatic moisture deficit (mm) (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - DDsub0: Degree-days below 0°C (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - DDsub18: Degree-days below 18°C (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - DD18: Degree-days above 18°C (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - DD5: Degree-days above 5°C (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - eFFP: End of the frost-free period (day of year) (annual)
  
  - EMT: Extreme minimum temperature over 30 years (°C) (annual)
  
  - Eref: Hargreaves reference evaporation (mm) (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - EXT: Extreme maximum temperature over 30 years (°C) (annual)
  
  - FFP: Frost-free period (mm) (annual)
  
  - MAP: Mean annual precipitation (mm) (annual)
  
  - MAT: Mean annual temperature (°C) (annual)
  
  - MCMT: Mean coldest month temperature (°C) (annual)
  
  - MSP: Growing season (May to September) precipitation (mm) (annual)
  
  - MWMT: Mean warmest month temperature (°C) (annual)
  
  - NFFD: Number of frost-free days (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - PAS: Precipitation as snow (mm) (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - PPT: Precipitation (mm) (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - RH: Relative humidity (%) (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - SHM: Summer heat/moisture index (annual)
  
  - Tave: Mean temperature (°C) (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - TD: Continentality (MWMT-MCMT) (°C) (annual)
  
  - Tmax: Mean daily maximum temperature (°C) (annual, seasonal, monthly)
  
  - Tmin: Mean daily minimum temperature (°C) (annual, seasonal, monthly)
